prompt.context: Our client is Healthy Foods Co., a wholesaler serving a variety of clients with food products. The client is profitable but they want you to help them find revenue growth opportunities from their current business.
prompt.question: How can we help Healthy Foods Co. drive their revenue growth?

clarifying_info.a: The client serves various customer categories including independent restaurants, chain restaurants, hospitals, school cafeterias, grocery stores, and others. Revenue by customer type is shown in Exhibit 1.

clarifying_info.q: What do customers care about most?
clarifying_info.a: Customer sensitivities ranked highest to lowest: price, convenient delivery, help with location planning, help with menu, website development, inventory, and help with management optimization.
The client is one of the market leaders and is not losing market share.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's share of wallet across customer types?
clarifying_info.a: Exhibit 2 shows share of wallet by customer type. Some customers classify the client as a primary supplier; for others the client is one of many.

clarifying_info.q: What is the wallet size for the smaller-revenue-generating customer segments?
clarifying_info.a: Exhibit 3 plots wallet size vs. the client's current share of wallet for the smaller-revenue-generating customer categories.

exhibits.title: Total Market Revenues by Customer Type
exhibits.shows: A breakdown of Healthy Foods Co.'s revenues by customer type
exhibits.data: Customer types listed: Independent restaurants (largest segment), Chain restaurants, Hospitals, School cafeterias, Grocery stores, Other

exhibits.title: Client's Share of Wallet
exhibits.shows: A chart showing the client's share of wallet (0–80%) across different customer types, labelled A, B, C, X by profitability (A highest, X lowest), with a dividing line indicating whether the client is a primary supplier or one of many
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Share of Wallet 0–80; Customer labels: A, B, C, X (A=highest profitability, X=lowest); threshold line separating 'Client is Primary Supplier' from 'Client is One of Many'

exhibits.title: Wallet Size vs. Share of Wallet
exhibits.shows: A scatter plot of wallet size ($M) vs. the client's share of wallet (%) for the smaller-revenue-generating customer categories
exhibits.data: X-axis: Share of Wallet 0–60%; Y-axis: Wallet Size $0–600M; Data points: Hospitals (large wallet ~$500M, low share ~10%), Hotels (large wallet ~$400M, low share ~20%), School cafeterias (mid wallet, mid share), Grocery stores (mid wallet, mid-high share), Chain restaurants (smaller wallet, higher share)

framework: Identify current customer mix and revenue contribution by customer type (Exhibit 1)
Assess share of wallet per customer type to understand penetration vs. growth headroom (Exhibit 2)
For customer types where share of wallet is already high, growth potential is limited — focus shifts to lower-share segments
Prioritize lower-share customer types by wallet size: the larger the wallet and the smaller the client's current share, the greater the revenue growth opportunity (Exhibit 3)
Develop targeted go-to-market strategies for the highest-potential segments, aligning offerings to their top sensitivities

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 1, what do you observe about the current revenue mix and what does it imply for growth?
questions.guidance: The candidate should note that independent restaurants are the largest revenue source. A strong candidate will resist the temptation to focus only on the largest segment and will instead ask whether there is headroom to grow there — prompting the need for share-of-wallet data.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, what can you conclude about the growth opportunities in the higher-revenue customer categories?
questions.guidance: The candidate should observe that share of wallet is already high (client is primary supplier) for the high-profitability, high-revenue customers (e.g., independent restaurants). This means growth in those segments is limited. The insight is to redirect attention to lower-revenue, lower-share-of-wallet customer types where there is room to grow.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, which customer segments represent the best revenue growth opportunity, and why?
questions.guidance: The candidate should frame a prioritization criterion: the ideal target has (1) a large total wallet and (2) a low current share for the client. From the scatter plot, hospitals and hotels stand out — both have large wallets (~$400–500M) and the client currently holds only a small share (~10–20%). The candidate should then suggest how to capture share there, linking back to customer sensitivities (e.g., convenient delivery, menu help, inventory management).

brainstorming.prompt: How should Healthy Foods Co. increase its share of wallet with hospitals and hotels?

categories.name: Service & Delivery
ideas: Offer dedicated delivery windows that fit hospital/hotel operational schedules
Provide same-day or next-day replenishment to minimize storage needs
Assign dedicated account managers for large institutional clients

categories.name: Product & Menu
ideas: Develop specialized product lines meeting hospital dietary/nutrition standards
Offer customized menu-planning consulting for hotel kitchens
Bundle specialty or seasonal items relevant to hotel F&B programs

categories.name: Technology & Convenience
ideas: Provide an online ordering portal with inventory tracking
Offer EDI integration with hospital procurement systems
Build a mobile app for easy reorder and delivery tracking

categories.name: Pricing & Contracts
ideas: Offer volume-based discounts to incentivize consolidating spend
Negotiate multi-year supply contracts with price locks
Provide flexible payment terms aligned with institutional billing cycles

categories.name: Relationships & Trust
ideas: Obtain relevant food safety certifications valued by hospitals
Demonstrate cost-savings case studies to procurement teams
Engage dietitians and F&B directors as key decision-makers

recommendation: Healthy Foods Co. should prioritize revenue growth in the hospital and hotel customer segments, where wallet sizes are large (~$400–500M) but current share of wallet is low (~10–20%), presenting the largest addressable growth opportunity

The client should tailor its service offering to the top sensitivities of these segments — particularly convenient delivery, menu help, and inventory support — to displace incumbent suppliers and become the primary provider
risks: Institutional procurement processes (hospitals, hotels) can be long and complex, extending the sales cycle
Competitors may respond aggressively if they perceive the client encroaching on their accounts
Cost of serving institutional clients (compliance, specialized products) may compress margins if not priced appropriately
next_steps: Conduct detailed interviews with hospital and hotel procurement teams to validate sensitivities and identify key decision-makers
Quantify the revenue upside by segment (wallet size × addressable share gain) to build the business case
Pilot an enhanced service model (e.g., dedicated account team + online ordering) with 2–3 target accounts before scaling
